title: Luyện Đọc VSTEP: Renewable Energy: Promise and Challenges (VstepR6-Test 02)

tasks.instructions: Directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.

passage.title: Renewable Energy: Promise and Challenges
passage.text:
The global transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy represents one of the most significant shifts in human history. Solar, wind, hydroelectric, and geothermal energy offer the promise of clean, sustainable power that does not produce the greenhouse gas emissions responsible for climate change. In recent decades, the cost of solar panels and wind turbines has fallen dramatically, making renewable energy increasingly competitive with traditional sources such as coal and natural gas.

Despite these advances, the transition faces considerable challenges. One major obstacle is intermittency: solar panels only generate electricity when the sun shines, and wind turbines only operate when the wind blows. This variability requires either large-scale energy storage systems, such as batteries, or the continued operation of conventional power plants as backup. Current battery technology, while improving rapidly, remains expensive and limited in its capacity to store energy for extended periods.

Another challenge is the infrastructure required to transmit renewable energy from where it is produced to where it is consumed. Solar farms are often located in remote desert regions, while wind farms are typically found in coastal or rural areas far from population centers. Building the transmission lines needed to connect these sources to cities requires enormous investment and can face opposition from local communities.

The economic and social dimensions of the energy transition are also significant. Fossil fuel industries employ millions of workers worldwide, and rapid changes in energy policy can threaten their livelihoods. Governments must therefore balance the urgent need to reduce carbon emissions with the equally important goal of ensuring a "just transition" that supports affected workers. Some nations have established retraining programs and economic diversification strategies to help manage this process.
